global_caption: The video contains 4 shots. It is an action-oriented sports short film in warm-toned pixel art style, set on a temporary golf fairway beside a pine forest by the sea. The overall lighting features golden sunset side light and natural ambient illumination.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a medium-long shot at eye level. Composition places the dark green edge of the pine forest in the left rear, with distant sea and beach faintly visible on the right. The foreground features pixelated grass bent by sea breeze, with a teacup with limbs standing on the grass at the forest edge as the visual focus. Shallow depth of field slightly softens the background horizon. The ceramic cup body is highlighted by warm golden side light, creating soft glowing edges, with highlights shimmering along the rim and handle. Its feet are firmly planted apart on the grass, the handle-like arm gripping the club and adjusting angle, body slightly lowered into a ready stance. Grass blades and tiny sand particles tremble gently in the wind, conveying stable tension before action. The The camera performs a very slight push-in, enhancing the sense of concentration before release.
shot2: Shot 2 connects with a hard cut from the previous shot, switching to a close-up at a slightly low-angle upward view. Focus locks onto the upper half of the teacup and the club. Foreground shows grass tips bent by wind, while the background features golden sea mist and pine forest rendered into simplified pixel blocks. Side lighting remains consistent, but the clubhead highlight becomes brighter at the moment of swing. The teacup’s handle-like arm swings powerfully, torso rotating smoothly, legs pushing off to shift weight, ceramic body showing slight vibration, shadow edges resembling cloth flaps and grass fragments being flung out to convey speed. A pixelated clubhead trail clearly forms in the air, creating a golden motion blur arc. In The camera rapidly pushes in along the swing path with slight lateral tracking, intensifying the explosive feel.
shot3: Shot 3 again connects via a hard cut, transitioning to a close-up tracking shot of the white ball. It combines overhead and lateral tracking, focusing on the flight arc of the white ball above the sandy beach. Below, the sand surface is dyed orange-gold by sunset, distant seawater advances in regular pixelated ripples, and background pines and coastline are compressed into thin layers. Shallow depth of field keeps the ball always sharpest, with occasional tiny pixel particles flashing in the surrounding air, emphasizing high-speed motion. The ball quickly rises from bottom-left to top-right, then begins descending, trajectory smooth without frame skips. Lighting maintains warm sunset tones, with a brief bright reflection appearing on the ball’s surface during rotation. The camera first pans to follow the ball, then subtly adjusts pitch to fully capture the arc peak and descent trend.
shot4: Shot 4 enters the final segment via a hard cut with slight speed matching, arriving at the seaside hillside green. It opens with a long-to-medium shot at eye level. Foreground features gently undulating pixelated grass slope, background sea reflecting continuous gold-orange glimmers under sunset. Overall shape is still formed by natural warm light and side-backlighting. The white ball drops from the top of the frame onto the green, bounces once, then rolls toward the flagstick. Grass texture forms a clear directional guide along the roll path, eventually stopping steadily just short of the hole. The teacup completes a crisp follow-through, body shifting from tension to relaxation, cup rim slightly lifted, expressing light joy and satisfaction after success. Wind continues to flutter the flag and grass tips, linking action outcome and environmental response naturally. The exact moment the ball stops aligns precisely with a brief silence in The camera first pulls back slightly to establish full green view, then slowly pushes toward the flagstick and stopped ball, settling the ending in openness.
